title_en: Qinyang City People's Procuratorate of Henan Province v. Yu Ping — case of intentionally disclosing state secrets
keywords_en: criminal; crime of intentionally divulging state secrets; first instance; basic people's court; Henan Province; natural person; Criminal Law; whether a lawyer allowing family members to review case files constitutes intentional disclosure of state secrets; dismissal of claims; lawyer's defense; disclosure of case files; false evidence; adjournment of trial; corruption
full_text_en:
Qinyang City People's Procuratorate, Henan Province v. Yu Ping — dispute over intentionally divulging state secrets

[Ruling Summary]

A lawyer who, while serving as defense counsel for a criminal defendant, allows the relatives of the party to review case evidence materials obtained through legal procedures, does not constitute the crime of intentionally divulging state secrets.

Procuratorial Authority: Qinyang City People's Procuratorate, Henan Province.

Defendant: Yu Ping, female, director of Jiaozuo Lutong Law Firm, Henan Province. Arrested on January 8, 2001.

The case of defendant Yu Ping for intentionally divulging state secrets was initiated by Qinyang City People's Procuratorate, Henan Province, which filed a public prosecution with Qinyang City People's Court, Henan Province on March 15, 2001.

Indictment Charges: On August 21, 2000, defendant Yu Ping, together with assistant lawyer Lu Xin (dealt with in a separate case), jointly served as defense counsel at first instance for Ma Minggang in his embezzlement case. On November 3 of the same year, Yu Ping, in preparation for court defense, arranged for Lu Xin to go to Qinyang City People's Court to photocopy the relevant case file materials of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case. After learning of this, Ma Minggang's relatives requested Lu Xin to allow them to view the photocopied materials. Following a telephone consultation with Yu Ping, Lu Xin left the photocopied materials with Ma Minggang's relatives, Zhu Kerong, Ma Mingkui, and others. That evening, Zhu Kerong, Ma Feng, and Ma Mingkui thoroughly reviewed the photocopied case file materials and conducted research against the indictment. The next day, based on the circumstances reflected in the case file materials, Zhu Kerong searched for and contacted relevant witnesses one by one, and carried out persuasion efforts. Later, when Yu Ping went to Qinyang to conduct investigations and collect evidence, witnesses Zhang Yuntian, Lü Xueqi, and others all produced false witness statements. At the same time, Zhu Kerong, based on some of the photocopied case file materials given to him by Yu Ping, found witness Wang Quansheng and persuaded him, resulting in Wang Quansheng also producing a false witness statement. Due to Yu Ping's intentional disclosure of state secrets, during the court hearing of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case, relevant witnesses gave false testimony, disrupting normal litigation activities, leading to the serious consequence of two adjournments of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case. The prosecutorial authority believed that defendant Yu Ping's conduct violated the provisions of Article 398 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law) and constituted the crime of intentionally divulging state secrets.

Defendant Yu Ping's Defense: She argued that she did not hand over the photocopied case file materials to Zhu Kerong on November 11; Lu Xin's act of leaving the photocopied case file materials with Zhu Kerong was a misunderstanding of her instructions. Furthermore, the case file materials photocopied by Lu Xin from the court were not marked as state secrets, and therefore her conduct did not constitute a crime.

Defense Counsel's Arguments: (1) The appraisal authority's conclusion that the case file materials photocopied by Lu Xin constituted state secrets, based solely on the relevant provisions of the procuratorial authority, was insufficiently justified. During the litigation stage, the case file materials of the procuratorial authority should be considered court litigation document materials, not state secrets. (2) The main witnesses in this case were Lu Xin, Zhu Kerong, Ma Mingkui, and others. Although Lu Xin was dealt with in a separate case, he should still be considered a co-defendant, and his statements of facts could not exclude the possibility of shifting responsibility; although Zhu Kerong, Ma Feng, and Ma Mingkui were present at the time, they could not have heard the content of Yu Ping's telephone conversation, so the above testimonies should not be admitted. (3) Although there was testimony from Zhu Kerong regarding whether Yu Ping handed over the case file materials to him, it was uncorroborated evidence and could not prove the existence of the fact. (4) Whether the testimonies of the relevant witnesses in Ma Minggang's case constituted false testimony could not be verified. The two adjournments were due to insufficient evidence by the prosecutorial authority requiring supplementary investigation; Yu Ping did not engage in conduct disrupting normal litigation activities. In summary, Yu Ping did not have the fact of intentionally divulging state secrets and should be acquitted.

Facts Found by Qinyang City People's Court:

On August 21, 2000, Yu Ping, a lawyer at Jiaozuo Lutong Law Firm, Henan Province, and assistant lawyer Lu Xin accepted the entrustment of Zhu Kerong, the wife of Ma Minggang, who was suspected of committing the crime of embezzlement, to serve as defense counsel at first instance for Ma Minggang's case. On November 1, 2000, Qinyang City People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against Ma Minggang for embezzlement and transferred to Qinyang City People's Court six volumes of copies of the main evidence in the case, totaling 421 pages. On November 3 of the same year, after learning that the case had been brought to court, Zhu Kerong informed Yu Ping. That afternoon, Yu Ping arranged for Lu Xin to come to Qinyang, and together with Ma Minggang's relatives Zhu Kerong, Ma Feng, Ma Mingkui, and others, they went to the Case Filing Division of Qinyang City People's Court. After going through the relevant procedures as required, Lu Xin borrowed and photocopied all the volumes of the main evidence in Ma Minggang's embezzlement case that had been transferred by the procuratorial authority to the court. After photocopying, Zhu Kerong requested Lu Xin to allow him to view the photocopied case file materials. Lu Xin did not agree and replied that he needed to seek Yu Ping's approval. Subsequently, Ma Mingkui used his mobile phone to call Yu Ping and requested to view the photocopied materials. Yu Ping agreed, instructed Ma Mingkui to hand the phone to Lu Xin, and told Lu Xin over the phone to leave the photocopied materials. Following Yu Ping's instructions, Lu Xin left the photocopied case file materials and returned to Jiaozuo. That evening, Zhu Kerong and others studied the indictment and the case file materials. The next day, Ma Feng went to Jiaozuo to return the photocopied case file materials to Lu Xin. Based on the circumstances reflected in the case file materials, Zhu Kerong contacted the relevant witnesses one by one and carried out persuasion efforts. On November 8 and 10 of the same year, when Yu Ping came to Qinyang to conduct investigations and collect evidence, witnesses Zhang Yuntian, Lü Xueqi, Hou Qinggang, and others involved in Ma Minggang's embezzlement case all produced false witness statements.

On November 11, 2000, after defendant Yu Ping had conducted investigations and collected evidence in Qinyang and was returning to Jiaozuo, because she had failed to obtain testimony from Wang Quansheng (a witness involved in the case file materials), she again left the photocopied case file materials with Zhu Kerong. On November 13, Zhu Kerong found Wang Quansheng and had Wang read Ma Minggang's confession. Based on Ma Minggang's confession, Wang Quansheng produced a false witness statement.

On November 15, 2000, at the public court hearing of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case, after defendant Yu Ping presented false testimonies and evidentiary materials from relevant witnesses, the prosecutorial authority twice proposed adjournment of the trial and decided to conduct supplementary investigation of Ma Minggang's case.

According to appraisals by the Henan Provincial State Secrets Bureau and Jiaozuo Municipal State Secrets Bureau, Henan Province, the case file materials of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case that defendant Yu Ping allowed Ma Minggang's family members to view were all classified as confidential state secrets.

The main evidence proving the above facts includes:

1. Testimony of witness Zhu Kerong. Main content: After Lu Xin had photocopied the case file materials at Qinyang City People's Court, she requested Lu Xin to allow her to view the case file materials. Lu Xin said that Yu Ping's consent was needed. After Lu Xin spoke with Yu Ping by phone, he left all the photocopied materials. She reviewed the materials that evening, and the next day went to find Zhang Yuntian, Lü Xueqi, and others to testify. On November 11, when Yu Ping came to Qinyang to collect evidence, because she had not found Wang Quansheng, she again asked Yu Ping to leave the case file materials. On the 13th, she found Wang Quansheng, had Wang review the materials concerning Ma Minggang in the case file, and had him write a relevant statement, which she then gave to Yu Ping.

2. Testimony of witness Ma Mingkui. Main content: After Lu Xin had photocopied the case file materials at Qinyang City People's Court, Zhu Kerong and he requested to view the photocopied case file materials and asked Lu Xin to leave the photocopied materials. Lu Xin did not agree, saying that Yu Ping's consent was required. He then contacted Yu Ping by mobile phone, and Yu Ping agreed over the phone. He then handed the mobile phone to Lu Xin, and after Lu Xin spoke with Yu Ping, he left the photocopied case file materials. That evening, at Zhu Kerong's home, he, Zhu Kerong, and Ma Feng carefully reviewed the photocopied case file materials.

3. Testimony of witness Ma Feng. Main content: Lu Xin photocopied the case file materials at Qinyang City People's Court and then left the materials. He reviewed the photocopied case file materials that evening, and the next day went to Jiaozuo to return the photocopied materials to Lu Xin.

4. Testimony of witness Wang Quansheng. Main content: Zhu Kerong found him and asked him to testify for Ma Minggang. At that time, Zhu Kerong was holding a bound volume of materials, and had him review the relevant passages.

5. Testimonies of witnesses Zhang Yuntian, Hou Qinggang, and others. They respectively proved that Zhu Kerong had requested them to provide relevant evidentiary materials to the lawyer for Ma Minggang.

6. Appraisals by Henan Provincial State Secrets Bureau and Jiaozuo Municipal State Secrets Bureau, Henan Province. They respectively proved that the case file materials of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case disclosed by Yu Ping were all classified as confidential state secrets.

Qinyang City People's Court held:

Article 398 of the Criminal Law provides: "Any functionary of a state organ who, in violation of the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Guarding State Secrets, intentionally or negligently divulges state secrets, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention; if the circumstances are especially serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years and not more than seven years."

Defendant Yu Ping, as a functionary of a state organ, while accepting entrustment from the family members of a criminal defendant to serve as defense counsel and relying on her unique status and authority as a lawyer, after becoming aware of the confidential materials related to the procuratorial authority's investigation of a criminal offense, divulged the state secrets she knew to the family members of the criminal defendant who were not supposed to know such secrets, thereby enabling the family members of the criminal defendant to have the opportunity to persuade witnesses to give false testimony. Due to Yu Ping's disclosure of a large amount of case file materials, normal litigation activities were seriously disrupted, the circumstances were serious, and her conduct constituted the crime of intentionally divulging state secrets. The facts of the prosecution's charge that Yu Ping committed the crime of intentionally divulging state secrets were clear, the evidence was sufficient, the charge was accurate, and it should be affirmed. The testimonies of the witnesses in this case, including Lu Xin, Zhu Kerong, Ma Mingkui, and Ma Feng, corroborated each other with the documentary and physical evidence. Yu Ping's defense that she did not engage in or instruct others to engage in conduct of divulging state secrets could not be established. Yu Ping's intentional disclosure of secrets led to a large amount of false evidence appearing during the court investigation of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case, causing the prosecutorial authority to twice apply for adjournment of the trial and conduct supplementary investigation, which seriously interfered with normal litigation activities, and the circumstances were serious. The defense counsel's argument that Yu Ping's conduct did not constitute serious circumstances was clearly inconsistent with the facts of the case and was therefore not adopted.

Accordingly, Qinyang City People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 19, 2001:

Defendant Yu Ping committed the crime of intentionally divulging state secrets and was sentenced to one year of fixed-term imprisonment.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, Yu Ping refused to accept it and appealed to Jiaozuo Intermediate People's Court, Henan Province.

Yu Ping argued in her appeal: She did not instruct Lu Xin to hand over the photocopied case file materials to the relatives of the party, nor did she hand over the case file materials to Zhu Kerong; the case file materials photocopied by Lu Xin were not marked as state secrets by any entity, nor was she informed by anyone in any form that they were state secrets. The prosecutorial authority's reliance on a post-event appraisal to claim that the case file materials were confidential state secrets was insufficiently justified and could not be used as evidence. She requested the reversal of the original judgment and a verdict of acquittal.

Defense Counsel argued: (1) Yu Ping's conduct had not reached the degree of serious circumstances. The two adjournments requested by the prosecutorial authority in Ma Minggang's embezzlement case were due to insufficient evidence for the charges requiring supplementary investigation, not because the witness testimony presented by Yu Ping contradicted the witness testimony presented by the prosecutorial authority. Therefore, Yu Ping's conduct did not disrupt or affect normal litigation activities. (2) Yu Ping was not a functionary of a state organ. The judgment of first instance's determination that Yu Ping was a functionary of a state organ and its application of Article 398, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law as the basis for sentencing constituted an improper application of the law. (3) Yu Ping did not have the subjective intent to divulge state secrets. Throughout the entire litigation process of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case, no one informed Yu Ping that the confessions and testimonies in Ma Minggang's embezzlement case file were state secrets that could not be disclosed to others, nor did the relevant authorities mark the confessions and testimonies in the case file with any classification level. (4) The appraisal by Jiaozuo Municipal State Secrets Bureau could not serve as the basis for determining the case. This appraisal was primarily based on the "Provisions on the Specific Scope and Classification Levels of State Secrets in Procuratorial Work" issued by the Supreme People's Procuratorate and its appendix "Provisions on Determining the Classification Level and Secrecy Period of Procuratorial Litigation Documents," which are confidential-level documents used by the procuratorial authority to regulate internal confidentiality work and are not binding on external persons. The court of first instance's reliance on this appraisal to determine that Yu Ping constituted the crime of intentionally divulging state secrets lacked legal basis.

Jiaozuo Intermediate People's Court found through trial:

The fact that Yu Ping, during her tenure as defense counsel at first instance for Ma Minggang, who was suspected of committing the crime of embezzlement, telephonically instructed assistant lawyer Lu Xin on November 3, 2000, to hand over photocopies of case file materials to Ma Minggang's relatives for review was clear. Regarding this, the evidence admitted by the court of first instance was legally sourced, its content was true and objective, and it should be affirmed.

Jiaozuo Intermediate People's Court held:

In this case, the case file materials that appellant Yu Ping allowed Ma Minggang's relatives to review were materials that she, in the performance of her duties as a lawyer, had photocopied from the case file of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case in court through lawful procedures. Although these materials were classified as confidential state secrets under the confidentiality provisions of the procuratorial authority, after the case entered the trial stage, the trial authority did not classify the evidence materials transferred by the procuratorial authority along with the case as state secrets. Yu Ping was not a functionary of a state organ, nor did she fall under the category of persons who are informed of state secrets as referred to in the confidentiality provisions of the procuratorial authority. As defense counsel for a criminal defendant, Yu Ping was not obligated to keep the case evidence materials that the court had permitted her to photocopy as state secrets. The procuratorial authority did not indicate a classification level on the case files it transferred; throughout the entire litigation process, no one informed Yu Ping that the case file materials of Ma Minggang's embezzlement case were state secrets that could not be disclosed to Ma Minggang's relatives, and therefore it could not be proven that Yu Ping knew these materials were state secrets and intentionally divulged them. Consequently, Yu Ping's conduct of allowing the relatives of the party to review case file materials obtained through lawful procedures during her tenure as defense counsel did not constitute the crime of intentionally divulging state secrets. The reasons for defense and arguments of Yu Ping and her defense counsel that no crime was committed were valid and should be adopted. The basic facts found in the original judgment were clear, the trial procedures were lawful, but the application of law was erroneous and should be corrected.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 189, paragraph (2) and Article 162, paragraph (2) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Jiaozuo Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on May 23, 2002:

1. The criminal judgment of first instance rendered by Qinyang City People's Court is reversed;
2. Appellant Yu Ping is acquitted.

This judgment is final.
